name: Alpine Climbing
description: A fast, self-sufficient style that combines rock, ice, and snow climbing over long routes, typically completed in a single push with minimal gear.

name: Rock Climbing
description: Climbing exposed rock faces using hands and feet, ranging from short bouldering problems to multi-day big wall ascents.

name: Ice Climbing
description: Ascending frozen waterfalls, ice-covered rock, and glaciers using ice axes and crampons for purchase on vertical or near-vertical ice.

name: Sport Climbing
description: Climbing routes protected by permanently fixed bolts, allowing climbers to focus on movement and technique rather than placing protection.

name: Traditional Climbing
description: Climbers place and remove their own protection in natural rock cracks and features as they ascend, leaving no permanent hardware behind.

name: Bouldering
description: Short, powerful climbing sequences performed without ropes close to the ground, usually with crash pads for protection.

name: Expedition Climbing
description: Large, logistically complex climbs involving multiple camps, fixed ropes, and extended time at altitude, often on the world's highest peaks.

name: High-Altitude Mountaineering
description: Climbing at extreme elevation where reduced oxygen, cold, and weather create severe physiological and logistical demands on the body.
